title: Precision Loss in Decimal Normalization Round Trip
description: Decimal truncation occurs when denormalizing payment amounts for tokens with fewer than 18 decimals. The rounding consistently favors claimers, as fractions are truncated down.
impact: Dust amounts are lost per claim transaction. The impact is systematic but negligible in practice - each claim loses at most 1 unit of the smallest decimal representation.
attackPath: Claimer calls claim() for a 6-decimal token
Claimer pays slightly less than the theoretical amount
Dust accumulates in protocol over many claims
recommendation: Consider rounding up instead of truncating to favor the protocol, or document this as intended behavior. For most practical purposes, the dust loss is acceptable.
